question: During a laparotomy under halothane anaesthesia, the patient develops rapidly rising end-tidal CO₂, HR 140 bpm, and generalised rigidity despite deepening anaesthesia. Which drug is immediately indicated?

answers.text: Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV — blocks RyR1 to halt the uncontrolled Ca²⁺ release causing malignant hyperthermia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This triad — hypercarbia, tachycardia, and rigidity under volatile anaesthesia — is malignant hyperthermia. Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV (repeat up to 10 mg/kg) blocks RyR1 on the sarcoplasmic reticulum, halting the pathological Ca²⁺ cascade. Simultaneously discontinue halothane and hyperventilate with 100% O₂.

answers.text: Atropine 1 mg IV to treat the tachycardia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The tachycardia is secondary to the hypermetabolic state, not the primary problem. Treating tachycardia alone ignores the catastrophic underlying pathology — uncontrolled Ca²⁺ release from skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum.

answers.text: Succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg IV to overcome the rigidity with complete paralysis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Succinylcholine is itself a known trigger of malignant hyperthermia and is absolutely contraindicated. Administering it would catastrophically worsen the crisis.

answers.text: Neostigmine IV to reverse any residual neuromuscular blockade causing the rigidity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is not residual neuromuscular blockade — it is MH-induced rigidity from sustained Ca²⁺ release via mutant RyR1 channels. Neostigmine has no effect on this peripheral pathology.

overallFeedback.feedback: MH triad: hypercarbia + tachycardia + rigidity under volatile anaesthesia. Treatment: discontinue the trigger agent, give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, hyperventilate with 100% O₂. Succinylcholine is absolutely contraindicated.
Well done. Dantrolene is the specific antidote for MH — it targets the exact pathological mechanism. Early recognition (hypercarbia + rigidity + tachycardia) and immediate treatment are life-saving.
